- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 3–5 days, model overreacts with high volatility; apply mean reversion to forecast, target 1–2% below recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay or exponential smoothing with decay factor 0.85 to reduce initial bias.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often misreads trend direction; align forecast with sentiment median rather than mean, especially if sentiment swings >0.2 over 3 days.
